- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 10–15% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward adjustment by 1–2 periods.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true +15%), apply mean reversion bias: subtract 5–10% from next 3 periods to reflect volatility decay.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.8) and forecast deviates >5% from true, adjust toward historical 18-day moving average for smoother transition.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early mean reversion (first 5–7 days), reduce forecast slope in early period to avoid lagged reaction.
